title.narrative: Reduction of the total water deficit in the target area

description.narrative: Difference between accessible supply (ex: springwater diverted to canals) and actual demand (total water use of farmers). This can be reduced both through supply augmentation (increased retention/storage) and demand management (improved practices/technologies).The water deficit is expressed for the whole AssiOrontes watershed including the mountain ranges on both sides of the Bekaa valley. The overall deficit figure will be desagregated into smaller subsystems such as the Labwe source watershed that is the main source of irrigation in the project area.An Integrated Water Resources study will provide information on the role of irrigation in the deficit and the possibilities to improve efficienct water use through improved management and through the use of nex techniques such as sprinklers and drips. The extension of the irrigation canal network that is foreseen in the project will increase the deficit. This extension will have to be countered with measures on the demand side, with the installation of buffer reservoirs for peak demand and possibly also with measures to reduce runoff of precipitation and to enhance the replenishment of underground aquifers.Cumulative impact of supply and demand side interventions against baseline value, recognizing but not accounting for externalities beyond the projects control.The original target value was calculated on the basis of the total water deficit of the Labwe Water Scheme as per USAID Master plan. However, on the one side, the length of the scheme in the master plan was inaccurate (it is in fact 172km as opposed to 109Km indicated in the master plan) and, on the other side, the project will target with rehabilitation works only a portion of the total scheme (22 Km out of 172 Km). The project is expected to reduce, on average, the water deficit of 37% of the 22Km which amounts to 1.56 Mm3/year

description.narrative: Difference between accessible supply (ex: springwater diverted to canals) and actual demand (total water use of farmers). This can be reduced both through supply augmentation (increased retention/storage) and demand management (improved practices/technologies).The water deficit is expressed for the whole AssiOrontes watershed including the mountain ranges on both sides of the Bekaa valley. The overall deficit figure will be desagregated into smaller subsystems such as the Labwe source watershed that is the main source of irrigation in the project area.An Integrated Water Resources study will provide information on the role of irrigation in the deficit and the possibilities to improve efficienct water use through improved management and through the use of nex techniques such as sprinklers and drips. The extension of the irrigation canal network that is foreseen in the project will increase the deficit. This extension will have to be countered with measures on the demand side, with the installation of buffer reservoirs for peak demand and possibly also with measures to reduce runoff of precipitation and to enhance the replenishment of underground aquifers.Cumulative impact of supply and demand side interventions against baseline value, recognizing but not accounting for externalities beyond the projects control.The original target value was calculated on the basis of the total water deficit of the Labwe Water Scheme as per USAID Master plan. However, on the one side, the length of the scheme in the master plan was inaccurate (it is in fact 172km as opposed to 109Km indicated in the master plan) and, on the other side, the project will target with rehabilitation works only a portion of the total scheme (22 Km out of 172 Km). The project is expected to reduce, on average, the water deficit of 37% of the 22Km which amounts to 1.56 Mm3/year
